# GALA

> GALA is a statically-typed, functional-first language that transpiles to Go. It has sealed types with exhaustive pattern matching, `Option`/`Try`/`Either` instead of `nil` and naked error pairs, immutability by default, and full Go interop. Source files are `.gala`; the compiler is `gala`.

GALA is close enough to Scala and Kotlin to be readable on sight, and different enough in specific places to trip a model writing from memory. The differences are listed below, with the compiler error each mistake produces. Every one of them is a hard compile error, not a lint — the build stops and names the fix.

## Getting the compiler to tell you

- `gala build ./main.gala` — compile; diagnostics carry a stable `GALA-Exxxx` code, a source span, and a fix hint
- `gala build --json ./main.gala` — the same diagnostics as JSON (`code`, `message`, `hint`, `file`, `line`, `column`, `endColumn`, `docsUrl`). Prefer this over parsing the framed text output
- `gala explain GALA-E0044` — the full reference page for a code, offline; `gala explain --list` enumerates them
- `gala run ./main.gala`, `gala test ./...`

## Differences that most often produce wrong code

- **Lambda parameters are always parenthesized.** `(x) => x * 2`, never `x => x * 2`. Applies to one parameter too. (`GALA-E0042`)
- **`match` is postfix.** `value match { case ... }`, not Rust's `match value { ... }`.
- **Methods are capitalized.** `.Map`, `.Filter`, `.Size` — not `.map`/`.filter`. `map` is additionally a reserved keyword, so `.map` fails in the parser.
- **Collections are built by named functions, never by calling the type.** `ArrayOf(1, 2, 3)`, `ListOf(...)`, `HashMapOf(("a", 1))`, `EmptyHashMap[K, V]()`. Scala's `List(1, 2, 3)` is an error. (`GALA-E0043`)
- **There is no `->` pair arrow.** A map entry is a tuple: `HashMapOf(("a", 1), ("b", 2))`.
- **No bare `len`, `append`, `make`, `panic`, `recover`.** Use `.Size()` (runes/elements) or `.ByteSize()` (bytes). (`GALA-E0035`)
- **No `defer`, no bare `go`.** Cleanup is `use` or `Using(res, (r) => ...)`; a goroutine is `go_interop.Spawn(() => f())`. (`GALA-E0036`)
- **No slice or map literals**, and Go slice/map *types* are legal only where a type is expected. (`GALA-E0007`, `GALA-E0008`, `GALA-E0040`)
- **No named `func` inside a function body.** A local helper is a lambda bound to a `val`: `val helper = (x int) int => x + 1`; for recursion, `var fact func(int) int` then assign. (`GALA-E0052`)
- **A type alias has no `=`.** `type Result[T any] Either[AppError, T]`, not Go's `type Result[T any] = Either[AppError, T]` (a parse error). An alias is the same type as its target, not a new type; a generic alias takes no methods, and a type that needs an identity or methods of its own is a struct. (`GALA-E0048`)
- **`val` is immutable and is the default.** Use `var` only when reassignment is genuinely needed.
- **Parameters, lambda parameters and receivers are immutable.** Reassigning `n` in `func f(n int)` or `(n) => ...` is an error; write `var n` to allow it. A receiver can never be rebound (no `var` receiver): copy it into a local `var`. Writing its `var` fields through it is fine.
- **No `val _ = expr`.** To drop a value, write the expression as a bare statement; in a lambda with no result, an `error`-only call becomes `FromError(call())`. (`GALA-E0060`)
- **Several values in one arm are alternatives, not Go's `case 1, 2:`.** Write `case 1 | 2 =>` or `case Some("a" | "b") =>`; `|` in a pattern is never a bitwise OR. Alternatives bind no names, so use `_` inside them. (`GALA-E0071`)
- **Sealed matches must be exhaustive.** Adding a variant turns every incomplete match site into a compile error naming the missing case — this is the property to lean on when refactoring. (`GALA-E0002`)
- **Prefer `Option`/`Try`/`Either` over `nil` and `(T, error)`.** Pattern-match to extract; do not call `.Get()` without checking. For a Go call returning only `error`, `Try(call)` (or `FromError(call)`) is a `Try[Void]` that fails on a non-nil error.
- **A Go call returning `(T, error)` is a `Try[T]`, not a `T`.** `val n = strconv.Atoi(s)` makes `n` a `Try[int]`; using it as an `int` is an error. Use `match { case Success(v) => ... case Failure(e) => ... }`, `.GetOrElse(default)`, `.Map(...)`, or `.Get()` (panics on failure); or bind Go-style with `val v, err = strconv.Atoi(s)`. Don't wrap it in `Try(...)` — that is the same `Try[int]`. A Go call returning `(A, B)` or more values is a Tuple: `val (k, v, found) = strings.Cut(s, "=")`. (`GALA-E0049`)
- **A function Go calls with several results declares Go's result list.** `func (c *Counter) Write(p []byte) (int, error)` implements `io.Writer`; its body gives a `Try[int]` (`Success(n)` or `Failure(err)`), and an `(A, B)` list takes a Tuple. A lambda passed as a Go `func() (T, error)` callback likewise gives a `Try`.
- **A codec decodes a struct with an unexported (lowercase) field only through `func (x T) Validate() Try[T]`.** `json.Codec[T]` / `yaml.Codec[T]` over such a struct — as the root, a field, or inside a collection — needs that exact method, which may simply return `Success(x)`; a codec over a struct of exported fields needs nothing. (`GALA-E0050`, `GALA-E0057`)
- **`type X Y` is an alias, not a newtype.** `X` and `Y` are one type, so a `Y` passes for an `X`, and `X` takes a method only when `Y` is a plain type (or a pointer to one) declared in the same package. For a distinct type with methods, declare `opaque type UserID int64`; the codec still writes it as the bare value. (`GALA-E0048`)
- **An `opaque type` never converts implicitly, and does not encapsulate.** Write `UserID(n)` and `int64(id)` explicitly (passing an `int64` for a `UserID` is `GALA-E0064`; `OrderID(userID)` is `GALA-E0063`, write `OrderID(int64(userID))`); untyped constants such as `42` still mix. Any package can convert, so a value that must be validated is `struct Email(v string)` with a constructor, not an opaque type. Its methods are not inherited from the underlying type: `opaque type Wait time.Duration` has no `.Seconds()`.
- **`case UserID(n)` unwraps exactly one value.** `n` is the underlying `int64`; `case UserID(a, b)` or `case UserID()` is `GALA-E0065`. An opaque type is not sealed, so a match on one ends in `case _`; a phantom-typed one matched on `any` spells its type arguments, `case Id[User](n)`.

## Shape of a program

```gala
package main

import . "martianoff/gala/collection_immutable"

sealed type Shape {
    case Circle(R float64)
    case Square(S float64)
}

func area(s Shape) float64 = s match {
    case Circle(r) => 3.14 * r * r
    case Square(a) => a * a
}

func main() {
    val shapes = ArrayOf(Circle(1.0), Square(2.0))
    val total = shapes.Map((s) => area(s)).FoldLeft(0.0, (acc, x) => acc + x)
    Println(s"total = ${total}")
}
```

`Println` and string interpolation (`s"..."`, `f"...%0.2f"`) are built in — no `fmt` import needed.

## Docs

- [Language reference](https://gala.fyi/docs/language-reference/): full syntax and semantics
- [Error codes](https://gala.fyi/docs/errors/): every `GALA-Exxxx`, with a repro, the real compiler output, and the fix
- [Examples](https://gala.fyi/docs/examples/): feature-by-feature programs
- [Immutable collections](https://gala.fyi/docs/immutable-collections/) · [Mutable collections](https://gala.fyi/docs/mutable-collections/): the method surface
- [Go interop](https://gala.fyi/features/go-interop/): calling Go, and where Go types are allowed
- [Go interop guide](https://gala.fyi/docs/go-interop/): mixing GALA and Go in both directions, mixed packages, building, using GALA from plain Go modules (`go.gala.fyi/stdlib`, `gala export`, `gala transpile --stdlib-module`), gotchas
- [Pattern matching](https://gala.fyi/features/pattern-matching/) · [Sealed types](https://gala.fyi/features/sealed-types/)
- [For AI agents](https://gala.fyi/for-ai/): why the compiler suits a generate-check-fix loop

- [Getting started](https://gala.fyi/docs/getting-started/): install and first program
